title: Trust-registry root isolation and rollback containment

scientific_lineage.summary: All preregistered P13-01..P13-16 endpoints executed on exact frozen head 1d251a52b8c2f7913b746de414f707bfbb9728fd and passed. The complete governed-platform governor suite passed 1010/1010. No post-exposure endpoint or mechanism repair was made.

supported_claim: On the tested same-host Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12 / OpenSSL prototype, trust-registry transition signing was moved into an isolated root-authority subprocess with separate durable replay/monotonic state. Registry readers pinned an exact root identity and public key, verified every event signature and predecessor/digest binding, and additionally required a separate monotonic trusted-minimum epoch plus event digest. Coherent rollback to historically valid root-signed registry snapshots below that minimum, unsigned coherent rewrites, root-id/public-key substitution, trusted-minimum rollback/rebinding, event deletion, transition-id semantic rebinding, and old-valid K1 reactivation were rejected on the exercised paths. Root outage blocked new registry mutation while already-issued valid history remained verifiable. Root restart preserved exact-transition replay and monotonic issuance memory. A clean K3-to-K4 transition remained live. Models, reviewers, checkpoint signers, writers, verifiers and ordinary registry surfaces gained no production, release, merge or approval authority from root signatures or registry verification.
observed_non_endpoint_hygiene: The frozen run emitted Python ResourceWarning messages for unclosed subprocess stdin/stdout TextIOWrapper handles in the Pilot 13 test/prototype process lifecycle. These warnings did not alter any P13 endpoint result or suite outcome and were not repaired post-exposure. They remain explicit cleanup debt rather than scientific-pass evidence.
not_proven: Protection after compromise or extraction of the Pilot 13 root private key
Secure recovery from a compromised root authority
Threshold or multi-root authorization for trust-registry transitions
Protection against same-user filesystem access, debugger, ptrace, process-memory inspection, host administrator, kernel, hypervisor or physical host compromise
implementation_note: The bounded prototype still persists the root private key in a same-host PEM file inside the root-authority directory. Process isolation plus a pinned public verification path is not evidence of root-key nonextractability. The separate trusted-minimum SQLite authority is also same-host and is not an independent administrative trust domain.
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 14: trust-registry root-key rotation and compromise recovery. Introduce externally governed root epochs and exact predecessor/root-transition binding so a historically valid but revoked root cannot authorize new registry history after rotation. Test clean R1-to-R2 rotation, post-revocation R1 signature rejection for current trust transitions, root-epoch rollback/stale-root replay, root-id/public-key substitution, transition-id replay and semantic rebinding across rotation, root outage/restart, concurrent old-root issuance versus rotation, and clean R2-to-R3 liveness. Keep root-trust mutation external to the root signer itself and do not claim independent administrative-domain or HSM/KMS guarantees.
